nodes.label: CF-02 — Dormant magnesium is drift evidence, never a candidate (P0)
nodes.norm_label: cf-02 — dormant magnesium is drift evidence, never a candidate (p0)
nodes.rationale: Shipping magnesium stays 1.8–2.4 context / 1.7–2.5 reference mg/dL. The retired biomarker_definitions row (5.2–6.5 optimal / 4.2–6.8 clinical) would be severe hypermagnesemia per the binding Lead A8 hazard statement; dormant numbers must never seed forward, are not a unit-conversion alternative, and no dormant range or candidate was added.

nodes.label: CF-07 — 'female on 76 entries' claim versus seed evidence (P1 metadata audit)
nodes.norm_label: cf-07 — 'female on 76 entries' claim versus seed evidence (p1 metadata audit)
nodes.rationale: The brief's claim of sex_applicability female on 76 entries is corrected: 76 is the unreviewed metadata count (44 female, 32 all) with seven analytes lacking a metadata row. No applicability value was changed to fit the brief and no default was promoted to an approval.

nodes.label: CF-08 — Additional definitions conflict: eGFR (P0)
nodes.rationale: Shipping eGFR 90–200 context / 60–200 reference mL/min/1.73m2 versus retired definitions 90–120 / 60–120 mL/min; no indexed/unindexed unit equivalence or conversion is asserted and no candidate was seeded. Needs both originating lab/equation specifications and a human adjudication of the unit and ceiling discrepancies.

nodes.label: Context modifiers and requires_context flag
nodes.rationale: Modifier order sex / age / cycle / pregnancy / life_stage (Q7). requires_context flags a review need, not a stratified value, and UNKNOWN never means irrelevant. Cycle flags derive from phase structure; other flags are offline analyte-class inferences. Missing stratification means an unphased row with at least one requires_context flag; existing stratification is still unverified.

nodes.label: eGFR (egfr)
nodes.rationale: P0, NEEDS_CONTEXT; context 90–200, reference 60–200 mL/min/1.73m2; specimen UNKNOWN (derived result). Historical ceiling conflict (200 versus 120) and indexed versus unindexed legacy units could change kidney-care interpretation (CF-08); equation, age scope and body-surface-area indexing are undocumented. Aliases: egfr; estimated gfr; glomerular filtration rate.

nodes.label: Female sex_applicability column default
nodes.rationale: female was the biomarker_catalog column default, not reviewed applicability evidence. The base seed has 76 unreviewed metadata entries (44 female, 32 all) plus seven analytes with no metadata row; the default is never grounds to label all 198 ranges female-adult.

nodes.label: lab_reference range kind
nodes.rationale: Mechanical mapping of the shipping 'clinical' band (Q6); supplies the clinical band used by status classification. DOUBTFUL as a genuine laboratory interval until an assay artifact establishes it, never to be presented as the patient laboratory range; review must separate reference intervals from clinical decision limits.

nodes.label: Magnesium (magnesium)

Owner-recorded severe serum hypermagnesemia hazard in the dormant 5.2–6.5 definition, which is permanently excluded from candidate selection (CF-02). Aliases: magnesium; mg.

It is not clinical approval: no external clinical source was retrieved, no clinical value changed, every source/URL/date/reviewer is null and every evidence grade is unsourced. Columns answer audit questions Q1 identity, Q2 specimen, Q3 unit/conversions, Q4 population, Q5 source/origin, Q6 kind verification, Q7 modifiers and Q8 review; requested artifacts have NOT been obtained.

nodes.label: Counters touched by regeneration
nodes.rationale: rate_limits 20/day, the introductory claims ledger, generation cost rows and up to two OpenAI calls; regeneration_count is client-incremented, client-writable and never enforced by the server.

nodes.label: Remediation implementation plan (T2 migration, T3 server, T4 client)
nodes.norm_label: remediation implementation plan (t2 migration, t3 server, t4 client)
nodes.rationale: Migration first, then a pure _shared/legacy-remediation.ts module behind an actions port that skips the 402 gate and ledger and forces claim authority, then a client handler shown only when the server reports remediation available.

nodes.label: Remediation proofs with killing mutations
nodes.rationale: Each proof (exact copy, free-row exclusion, untouched counters, no 402, byte-identical private row, current-policy version, provenance honesty, failure behaviour, no automatic writes, unchanged TASK-047 quarantine, unmixed columns, concurrency) names a mutation that must turn it red.

nodes.label: save_interpretation_remediation writer (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Service-role SECURITY DEFINER transaction that locks rows and re-verifies ownership, legacy status, deep depth, claim or premium basis and no existing version before inserting; it never writes interpretations_private, the ledger, Stripe or regeneration_count.

nodes.label: TASK-048 V2-03e Turn 1: Paid-Legacy Regeneration Investigation
nodes.norm_label: task-048 v2-03e turn 1: paid-legacy regeneration investigation

nodes.label: Destructive in-place regeneration overwrite (STOP condition)
nodes.rationale: Every Regenerate writer ends in INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (lab_report_id) DO UPDATE on the single interpretations_private row, replacing both bodies, provenance and generated_at under the same id with no history, so versioning must come before any $0 path.

nodes.label: Free legacy accidental-qualification predicates
nodes.rationale: Eligibility must never derive from flag-off access full, stored_depth deep alone, tier IN (plus, NULL) or any client-supplied flag, because each admits free, trial or complimentary rows.

nodes.label: No durable paid record for subscription-era rows
nodes.norm_label: no durable paid record for subscription-era rows
nodes.rationale: interpretations.tier is descriptive only and was written as plus for trial and complimentary users, and Stripe sells subscriptions only, so the introductory claim is the only durable report-level entitlement.

nodes.label: No server-side regeneration authorization
nodes.rationale: generate-interpretation authorizes every request the same way and never checks an existing interpretation, regeneration_count or legacy status; with freemium inactive withClaimAuthority is skipped, so a regenerated AI row is itself quarantined.

nodes.label: Option A: append-only interpretation_versions table (recommended)
nodes.rationale: A service-only table whose CHECKs require current claims keeps the legacy row's id, bytes, generated_at and provenance, satisfying the no-upgrade-in-place ruling and reusing at-rest proofs; ordinary writers must refuse to overwrite eligible rows.

nodes.label: Remediation eligibility predicate (v1)
nodes.rationale: legacy row AND deep AND no version AND (claim for report or blood draw OR flag-on premium viewer); mirrors the current read contract with no widening and is re-checked inside the write transaction.

nodes.label: Whole-tuple reader selection invariant
nodes.rationale: Readers return the version or the private row as one tuple, still through interpretation_read_quarantine, because mixing columns across the two would misattribute provenance.

nodes.label: Nutrient medical boundaries (educational, never prescriptive)
nodes.rationale: Core principles: mention nutrients only when tied to a specific lab value or reported symptom, frame every mention as a topic to discuss with a clinician, never give dosages, timing, frequencies or brands. nodes.norm_label: nutrient gating logic (include only when tied to an out-of-range lab value or correlated symptom)
nodes.rationale: Excludes general wellness advice, population statistics and preventive suggestions. The lab-value tie is semantic, not regex: the validator passes an untied magnesium mention, so only the system prompt rejects it.

nodes.label: Substance-context guard for prescriptive verbs and frequency terms
nodes.norm_label: substance-context guard for prescriptive verbs and frequency terms
nodes.rationale: Prescriptive verbs and frequency terms fire only when the same string carries a supplement/vitamin/pill/dose word, a dosage unit or a named nutrient. Without the guard, ordinary English ('take a hit', 'track your energy daily') would send clean reports to the non-AI fallback.

nodes.rationale: Whether Supabase's hosted postgres role can set the parameter is unverified vendor behaviour; H048-REPLICA-SET only proves anon, authenticated and service_role get 42501.

nodes.label: TASK-048 Turn 5: Guards That Survive Replica Mode
nodes.norm_label: task-048 turn 5: guards that survive replica mode
nodes.rationale: Settles the reviewers' disagreement about session_replication_role = replica by building and mutating rather than by argument; none of the new SQL was executed.

nodes.label: ENABLE ALWAYS guard trigger hardening
nodes.rationale: ALWAYS triggers still fire under replica mode, closing the bypass for any role that can set session_replication_role; firing during logical-replication apply is accepted because no publication or subscription exists and halting on divergence beats silently overwriting history. The table owner or a superuser who can disable or drop triggers remains a residual.

nodes.label: Recorder trigger deliberately left ORIGIN
nodes.rationale: If the recorder were ALWAYS and both tables were logically replicated, the recorder-inserted protection row would collide with the replicated one on the primary key and halt apply on legitimate traffic, with no protection gain; the only loss is the durable record for rows written in replica mode.

nodes.label: deleteDataTables (delete-user-data)
nodes.rationale: Root cause: four concurrent writers on one graph through Promise.all taking locks in opposite orders. Now awaits erase_reports once for all report ids before anything else; the per-report child deletes were removed because the cascade already empties them and a second writer would recreate the ordering hazard.

nodes.label: erase_reports(uuid[])
nodes.rationale: Service-only SECURITY DEFINER with search_path=pg_catalog,public; locks the reports ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE then deletes them, and the cascade removes children, history, protection, versions and pointers while claims keep their row with report_id NULL.

nodes.label: Account-deletion deadlock risk
nodes.rationale: delete-user-data runs delete_interpretations concurrently (Promise.all) with direct child-table deletes; the report cascade locks the same rows in a different order, so erasure can fail intermittently.

nodes.label: delete_interpretations rename plan (erase_reports)
nodes.rationale: Add service-only erase_reports, point delete-user-data at it with a deterministic ORDER BY id lock order, then make delete_interpretations raise; never alias a name that promises interpretation-only deletion while it erases raw results.

nodes.label: SQL-TypeScript blood-draw hash parity
nodes.rationale: The draw is sha256('sha256:' || lower(content_hash)) when a hash exists, else sha256('report:' || id) when there is no file; both directions are pinned by shared literals.

nodes.label: H048E-LOCK-ORDER static lock-order pin
nodes.rationale: A deadlock needs two connections and the SQL harness runs on one, so lock order is pinned statically and caller ordering is proven in TypeScript; no deadlock reproduction is claimed.

nodes.label: S2-08 Longitudinal insights

nodes.label: S2-09 Cross-marker pattern intelligence

nodes.label: S2-10 Personal-baseline intelligence

nodes.label: Observational, non-causal outcome language
nodes.rationale: Causal language is the trap: changes are described as observation over time, never cause and effect, and templates make no causal claim without authority.

nodes.label: Deterministic rules first, model prose only where authorized
nodes.norm_label: deterministic rules first, model prose only where authorized
nodes.rationale: Pattern detection is rule-based and testable; model prose is added only where an authorized fact supports it.

nodes.label: Personal comparison label (not a clinical range)
nodes.norm_label: personal comparison label (not a clinical range)

nodes.label: No new check-functions.sh exclusions
nodes.rationale: Never add an exclusion to docs/check-functions.sh; packets treat needing a new baseline exclusion as a stop condition.

nodes.label: Clinical authority rule
nodes.rationale: Amani is educational: no diagnosis, prescriptive advice, doses, frequencies, timing or brands; no new range, threshold or evaluative wording without an approved source; unmappable AI prose is suppressed; safety is decided deterministically, never by the model; Basic never gains replacement content; legacy interpretations stay quarantined and versions are append-only.

nodes.label: Honest reporting of pending checks
nodes.rationale: Anything that could not be run is reported as pending with the reason, never claimed as passed.

nodes.label: No secrets, names only
nodes.rationale: No secrets in code, logs, PRs or notes; refer to them by name only, for example OPENAI_API_KEY.

nodes.label: Owner-only actions rule
nodes.rationale: Merging, deploying, supabase db push, supabase functions deploy, Netlify settings, flags such as FREEMIUM_ACTIVE, live Stripe/IAP and store submission need explicit owner approval and are done by the owner.

nodes.label: Never silently resolve a [Pending]
nodes.rationale: When only the owner can answer, that part of the work stops and a question is added.

nodes.norm_label: pure _shared module behind an injected actions port
nodes.rationale: Server logic stays testable with Vitest fakes and the Deno handler stays thin; native plugins go only through src/lib/native.ts; Tailwind theme tokens and lucide-react only.

nodes.rationale: Credentials never go into the repo, chat or the Second Brain, where only variable names may appear.

nodes.norm_label: goal-driven verify loop (lint, typecheck, test, build)

The skill description and type-guard rule still speak of a no-test codebase, which is stale against the Vitest suite it describes.

nodes.rationale: Service only: 22023 for a NULL request or non-object provenance before the ledger; settles the claim, then appends a deep version in the same transaction so any writer refusal undoes the claim; limit_reached persists nothing; idempotent on request_id; never calls save_interpretation or touches the anchor.

nodes.label: interpretation-versions.ledger.sql (harness section 11)
nodes.rationale: H048L-* properties in both flag states, from first generation and the overwrite defect through column refusals, limit, idempotency, grants, guard enablement and a final static RPC-scope check.

nodes.label: introActions.commitDeepAccess ledger port
nodes.rationale: When appendsVersion is set the call goes to commit_deep_access_version keyed by request_id with the claim-authority body, its Basic projection and regeneration provenance; commit_deep_access_v2 is reached only without an anchor.

nodes.label: settle_introductory_claim
nodes.rationale: Internal, ungranted, the claim rules once: per-user advisory lock, ownership FOR UPDATE (23503), idempotency on draw or report (already_claimed), 22023 for an unclaimed report without consume, the three-claim limit (limit_reached) and the claim insert (committed); writes only the claim.

nodes.label: commit_deep_access RPC
nodes.rationale: Introductory-claim ledger writer that also upserts the interpretation and overwrites generated_at.

nodes.label: interpretations_private (historical source table)
nodes.rationale: Kept as the historical source: never rewritten, relabelled, stamped or reserialized; protected rows are frozen at the database boundary.

nodes.label: introductory_deep_access_claims table
nodes.rationale: Durable user plus blood-draw claim with optional report link; usable under H1 route 1 without billing proof or an active subscription.

nodes.label: persistIapSubscription
nodes.rationale: Replaces status, expiry and the raw provider payload on update, so no event history is retained.

nodes.label: save_interpretation RPC
nodes.rationale: Upsert writer that overwrites the stored body and generated_at: the destructive regeneration defect.

nodes.label: stripe-webhook edge function
nodes.rationale: Fetches only the latest subscription (limit 1) and upserts on customer_id, so renewals replace period and status fields.

nodes.label: Interpretation version foundation migration (20261010000000)
nodes.rationale: One-shot: replay raises an explicit already-applied error and rolls back, a prerequisite guard refuses out-of-order application, and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE is held from the ledger snapshot until the guard is installed.

nodes.label: interpretation_history_protection identity ledger
nodes.rationale: Filled at migration time and by the recorder; composite FK (interpretation_id, lab_report_id) prevents naming another report's or a missing interpretation; erasure cascades through it.

nodes.label: zz_guard_interpretation_history trigger / guard_interpretation_history()
nodes.rationale: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE guard comparing to_jsonb(NEW) with to_jsonb(OLD); freezes every column so relabel-then-overwrite and id changes fail; only byte-identical no-op updates pass.

nodes.label: evaluate_legacy_remediation
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER STABLE, service_role only: eligible only if the report is owned, holds a protected legacy AI row, and the user has a matching claim by report or derived draw; missing and foreign reports return one shape; never reads tier, depth, subscriptions, trial or promotional markers.

nodes.label: __verification__/prelude.sql lab_reports stand-in
nodes.rationale: Adds nullable file_url and regeneration_count (default 0) to match the initial schema, so the evaluator and the R-REGEN-COUNT mutation have the columns they touch.

nodes.label: First-generation race
nodes.rationale: Two concurrent first generations both see no anchor; from turn 11 the loser's upsert is refused with 55000 (409) and its transaction, claim included, rolls back instead of overwriting the winner.

nodes.label: Ledger in-place upsert defect (commit_deep_access_v2 on an anchored Free report)
nodes.norm_label: ledger in-place upsert defect (commit_deep_access_v2 on an anchored free report)
nodes.rationale: At c6c4ed2 an activated Free regeneration whose ledger committed upserted an un-versioned current-policy anchor in place because the guard refused only legacy or versioned anchors; reclassified from seam to defect by reviewer-10 and closed in turn 11.

nodes.label: L-* ledger killing mutations
nodes.rationale: L-RPC-SAVE, L-GUARD-JSON, L-SKIP-APPEND, L-LIMIT-IGNORED, L-SETTLE-LIMIT, L-SETTLE-IDEMPOTENCY, L-CDA-LIMIT-WRITE, grant mutations and L-GUARD-ORIGIN, each required to turn its probe red for the named reason.

nodes.label: Historical payment cannot be established from the retained model
nodes.norm_label: historical payment cannot be established from the retained model
nodes.rationale: Stripe keeps one upserted subscription snapshot per customer, orders have no report binding, event ledgers hold no invoice body, and IAP raw payloads are overwritten, so no durable report-specific paid proof exists.

nodes.label: Migration proof sequence (fresh chain, upgrade, replay, byte identity, rollback)
nodes.norm_label: migration proof sequence (fresh chain, upgrade, replay, byte identity, rollback)
nodes.rationale: JSONB byte comparison proves identity of the stored representation only, and replay must be an explicit contract rather than a no-op hidden by IF NOT EXISTS.

nodes.label: Separate remediation evaluator (design)
nodes.rationale: Eligible only through an existing claim for that user and report or the same trusted blood draw; the paid-proof branch has no safe implementation; never calls claim acquisition, commit_deep_access_v2, Stripe or the regeneration counter.

nodes.label: Current-policy rows still overwritten in place (H048-CURRENT-ROW-STILL-WRITABLE)
nodes.norm_label: current-policy rows still overwritten in place (h048-current-row-still-writable)
nodes.rationale: H3 scopes preservation to legacy AI rows, so ordinary regeneration of an un-versioned current-policy row keeps today's in-place writer.

nodes.label: Foundation killing mutations (GUARD, LEDGER, REMEMBER, TRUNCATE, GRAFT, DORMANT, ERASURE-RPC and others)
nodes.norm_label: foundation killing mutations (guard, ledger, remember, truncate, graft, dormant, erasure-rpc and others)
nodes.rationale: Each mutation runs inside an uncommitted transaction and must turn its named probe red with the quoted text; a surviving mutation fails the harness.

nodes.label: Legacy regeneration fails with 55000 in both flag states
nodes.norm_label: legacy regeneration fails with 55000 in both flag states
nodes.rationale: Without a remediation path save_interpretation raises 55000, the edge marks the report error and returns 500, and the client keeps the optimistic regeneration_count charge; the migration must not reach production ahead of the edge/client change.

nodes.label: 55000 to 409 legacy_history_protected mapping
nodes.rationale: A 55000 from save_interpretation or commit_deep_access_v2 on a protected row returns 409 without writing status='error', so preserved history is not branded as a failed report.

nodes.label: Unhashed-file eligibility narrowing
nodes.rationale: With no content_hash but a file, SQL cannot hash the file, so only the report_id match remains; this narrows eligibility relative to findClaim and fails closed rather than adding a write to an ineligible request.

nodes.label: claim.covered keys on the historical row's blood_draw_id (fixture rE)
nodes.norm_label: claim.covered keys on the historical row's blood_draw_id (fixture re)
nodes.rationale: Legacy rows saved without a draw have a NULL blood_draw_id, so a report remediated through a draw-matched claim is served Full by the POST but Basic on every later read; narrows access, widens nothing.

nodes.label: TASK-048 Turn 11: Close the Last In-place Writer
nodes.norm_label: task-048 turn 11: close the last in-place writer
nodes.rationale: Repair turn on base c6c4ed2 closing the defect at both layers: the application never persists an anchored report through commit_deep_access_v2 or save_interpretation, and the database refuses the overwrite even if it tried.

nodes.label: TASK-048 Turn 2: Historical Payment Evidence and Persistence Design
nodes.norm_label: task-048 turn 2: historical payment evidence and persistence design
nodes.rationale: Investigation and design only: separates immutable storage, current-version selection and remediation eligibility, and returns the missing historical-payment evidence contract for owner decision before any migration is written.

nodes.label: TASK-048 Turn 4: Persistence Foundation, Judged and Made Provable
nodes.norm_label: task-048 turn 4: persistence foundation, judged and made provable
nodes.rationale: Keeps the inherited owner-approved append-only schema because no defect justified a different design; fixes harness defects; every database property is an executable claim the Lead must run.

nodes.label: blood_draw_id fill-once exception
nodes.rationale: First generation inserts the anchor without a draw and save_interpretation fills it in the same transaction; changing a set draw would change the readers' claim coverage, so only the NULL fill is allowed. Residual: a direct service-role UPDATE can still fill a NULL draw later.

nodes.label: Protected column set on every interpretations_private row
nodes.norm_label: protected column set on every interpretations_private row
nodes.rationale: The guard refuses with 55000 any change to id, lab_report_id, json_output, interpretation_source, tier, generated_at, disclaimer_version, or a set blood_draw_id, on legacy and current-policy rows alike; projection columns stay writable because a projection change is not a body overwrite (residual: a service-role caller can still rewrite an anchor's Basic projection).

nodes.label: Erasure-safe report-graph deletion (design)
nodes.rationale: An unconditional DELETE-blocking trigger breaks report and account deletion, while an unrestricted delete RPC allows delete-and-reinsert; so a narrowly authorized operation deletes the report and its whole version/history graph atomically.

nodes.label: Database-boundary history protection guard (design)
nodes.rationale: Guard runs on the underlying private table so direct service writes and SECURITY DEFINER upserts are covered; classifies from OLD, freezes every column so relabel-then-overwrite fails, and keeps a durable protection identity across classifier changes.

nodes.label: Unknown payment attribution fails closed (H1)
nodes.rationale: Neither current Premium, tier, depth, legacy prose, a version row, a processed webhook nor a non-trial snapshot establishes a durable historical remediation right.

nodes.label: Report erasure does not refund claims
nodes.norm_label: report erasure does not refund claims
nodes.rationale: A claim keeps its row with the report link set to NULL and is erased only with the account.

nodes.label: Forward-only production rollback
nodes.rationale: The rollback script is a disposable pre-use rehearsal that refuses once versions exist; in production it would reopen the destructive overwrite, so stop serving and generating and keep guards, ledger and versions.

nodes.label: One-shot migration replay contract
nodes.rationale: Supabase applies each migration once; IF NOT EXISTS would turn a wrong or partial schema into a silent no-op, so replay must raise and roll back leaving the catalog byte-identical.

nodes.label: Protection as a union of three tests (ledger, live classifier, anchors a version)
nodes.norm_label: protection as a union of three tests (ledger, live classifier, anchors a version)
nodes.rationale: A classifier change can add protection but never remove it; the ledger keeps a legacy row protected even if a future classifier would accept it.

nodes.label: zz_ trigger naming for BEFORE ROW firing order
nodes.norm_label: zz_ trigger naming for before row firing order
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL fires same-event BEFORE ROW triggers in name order, so the guard runs after prepare_interpretation_projection and a future NEW-editing trigger cannot slip past; a trigger named after zz_guard remains a residual.

nodes.label: Medical boundaries (allow-list-first nutrient policy)
nodes.rationale: Supplementation language that names no allow-listed nutrient is itself a violation, so an unlisted supplement such as berberine, inositol or red clover fails closed instead of passing unnoticed.

nodes.label: Invariant 4: missing context withholds, no broad fallback (withhold rather than guess)
nodes.norm_label: invariant 4: missing context withholds, no broad fallback (withhold rather than guess)
nodes.rationale: Without a usable phase or under a non-cycling state Amani gives no status, no band and no fallback; the old wide general-range fallback turned progesterone 2.0 into 'optimal', a false reassurance.

nodes.label: Ruling R2: one authorized-language function (authorizedLanguage) and the SAFE-is-not-optimal trap
nodes.norm_label: ruling r2: one authorized-language function (authorizedlanguage) and the safe-is-not-optimal trap
nodes.rationale: SAFE does not authorize 'optimal': ClaimEvidence (optimal_target, favourable_direction) is kept separate from review, canDescribeAsOptimal needs a reviewed range plus optimal-target evidence, and the catalog records no claim evidence (NO_CLAIM_EVIDENCE). Unauthorized titles become '<subject> needs review'.

nodes.label: ClinicalObservation renderer
nodes.rationale: Revalidates claim-bearing sentences at render time and renders nothing for invalid proposals (defence in depth behind authorizeModelProse).

nodes.label: Claim-selection generation contract (Ask Amani shape)

nodes.label: Fail-closed exact phrase matching

nodes.norm_label: npm run check:functions (bash docs/check-functions.sh npx --yes deno@2)

nodes.norm_label: ci 'edge function typecheck' job (denoland/setup-deno@v2, deno v2.x)

nodes.label: V2-05-02: Deterministic critical-value engine
nodes.rationale: False negatives are the dangerous direction, so ties and boundary semantics are explicit per rule.

nodes.label: V2-05-03: Unit-sanity validation
nodes.rationale: Wrong-unit interpretation is a real harm path; conversions only where the catalog defines an approved factor.

nodes.label: V2-05-04: Pregnancy-specific red flags
nodes.rationale: Highest clinical sensitivity in the backlog; every rule needs clinical sign-off.

nodes.label: V2-05-05: Pre-generation safety enforcement
nodes.rationale: Safety content must not be paywalled, and the deterministic safety message survives model failure.

nodes.label: V2-05-06: Post-generation safety enforcement
nodes.rationale: The model is never the authority on safety.

nodes.label: V2-05-07: Safety-authority pathway in claims and UI
nodes.norm_label: v2-05-07: safety-authority pathway in claims and ui
nodes.rationale: Wording must avoid diagnosis while staying clear about urgency.

nodes.norm_label: v2-06-01: amanicontext type, schema and builder

nodes.rationale: Mis-merged series produce false trends.

nodes.norm_label: v2-06-08: wire amanicontext into generation and insights (data minimization)

nodes.rationale: Waits for 1.0.6 on both testing tracks, switches DB visibility ON and validates old 1.0.5 confidentiality before setting FREEMIUM_ACTIVE=true and then the web/client flag; a flagged-on Free request with visibility OFF logs the mismatch and rechecks legacy entitlement before ledger or model work, and config read errors yield 503. Rollback unsets the flags, then switches visibility OFF.

nodes.label: Rollout Milestone 3: Cutover (migrations 20260926000001 and 20260926000002)
nodes.rationale: Rehearse in a disposable database and verify live PostgREST select shapes, Basic/Full selection and cross-user denial on a preview project with real JWTs before GO, because raw SQL alone is insufficient; the rename keeps table OID, FK cascade, indexes, unique constraint and triggers. After cutover an old direct-upsert or direct-delete handler must never be redeployed.

nodes.label: Rollout Milestone 1: Prepare (migration 20260926000000)
nodes.rationale: Additive: Basic projection, stored depth, projection version and trusted draw ID columns, floor-only legacy backfill, the switch installed OFF, the legacy-writer trigger, service-only save/delete RPCs and commit v2; client mutation grants are revoked. Rollback leaves the schema and switch OFF and never restores authenticated writes.

nodes.label: Rollout Milestone 4: Read Endpoint (deploy get-interpretation, verify_jwt=true)
nodes.norm_label: rollout milestone 4: read endpoint (deploy get-interpretation, verify_jwt=true)
nodes.rationale: No old client calls it; validate TS sandbox+beta Full versus SQL Basic and structured retryable failures. Rollback withdraws the endpoint while old clients keep using the compatibility view.

nodes.label: Rollout Milestone 2: Writers (generate-interpretation, delete-user-data, guard consumers)
nodes.norm_label: rollout milestone 2: writers (generate-interpretation, delete-user-data, guard consumers)
nodes.rationale: Deploying before prepare is invalid; both generation write paths save Full and Basic in one transaction. Rollback before cutover may restore old functions because the compatibility trigger keeps their Basic projection fresh.

nodes.label: Projection Version 2
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes the repaired projection logic from the earlier unreleased logic; the column and its CHECK are the only record of the version after TASK-033 removed the unused PROJECTION_VERSION constant.

nodes.label: read_interpretation_for_server Projection-Selecting RPC
nodes.rationale: Takes the authenticated user ID and the TS-resolved premium boolean, enforces ownership again and returns only the selected body.

nodes.label: selectPremiumPreview Pure Contract
nodes.rationale: Cross-marker previews need at least two linked markers and trend/lifestyle previews at least one, none abnormal; a trend needs numeric delta or comparison evidence, unknown legacy provenance yields no preview, and ineligible previews still count as locked candidates.

nodes.label: checkUserSubscription strictReadErrors Opt-In for Guard Consumers
nodes.norm_label: checkusersubscription strictreaderrors opt-in for guard consumers
nodes.rationale: All four generation, extraction and comparison guard consumers opt into strict DB read errors while the fourth argument defaults false for existing callers; lab-insights returns 402 premium_required to Free users only after activation.

nodes.label: Trend Evidence Attachment (trend_evidence[], at most 8)
nodes.rationale: Activated generation records significant same-unit changes against the most recent earlier report using lab-insights' comparison rules, now in _shared/trend-evidence.ts; it adds a PRIOR-REPORT CHANGES prompt block only when evidence exists, needs no extra model call and is never part of the SQL floor. With the flag off the stored payload is byte-identical.

nodes.label: Interpretation Visibility Switch (singleton config, installed OFF)
nodes.norm_label: interpretation visibility switch (singleton config, installed off)
nodes.rationale: Stored in the service-only interpretation_visibility_config; the switch is the only intentional bypass (explicit false reproduces today's full payload for the owning user), and missing configuration is treated as protected, never OFF.

nodes.label: Interpretation Visibility Rollout (DARK, TASK-031)
nodes.rationale: Source changes imply no activation, deployment, merge or production verification; each milestone needs a separate owner GO and Lead evidence (migration files are not evidence of deployed state), no blanket supabase db push may cross the prepare/cutover boundary, and Fable and Opus adversarial reviews remain required.

nodes.label: delete-user-data Deletion Order (auth identity deleted last)
nodes.norm_label: delete-user-data deletion order (auth identity deleted last)
nodes.rationale: Refuses with 409 while an unacknowledged store subscription is still billing (paused counts, because Google resumes it); deletes Stripe data, the storage prefix and data rows before the auth.users identity so an earlier failure leaves the user able to sign back in and retry; iap_subscriptions rides ON DELETE CASCADE so a mid-flight failure cannot erase a paying customer's entitlement; every step throws so failure is never reported as success.

nodes.label: Deterministic Narrative Is Floor (TASK-033)
nodes.rationale: When the source is fallback or deterministic, Basic carries overall_interpretation and pattern_signals verbatim and those paths leave the preview pool; AI or unknown sources are unchanged.

nodes.label: Floor Migration Replay Hazard (20260926000003 after 20260927000001)
nodes.rationale: Re-applying 20260926000003 alone after 20260927000001 makes the one- and two-argument floor functions call each other, so every floor call fails with stack depth exceeded; the Supabase migration ledger prevents this and no repair script may bypass it.

nodes.label: Legacy Client Direct json_output Exposure
nodes.rationale: Legacy clients select interpretations.json_output directly, so storing a deep Free payload there would make its bodies downloadable regardless of UI state; the new facade therefore selects one projection at read time.

nodes.label: Legacy-Writer Projection Trigger
nodes.rationale: Keeps the Basic projection fresh for old writers so writer rollback stays safe before cutover; it writes projection version 2 and is made source-aware by migration 20260926000003.

nodes.label: Production Privilege Check Query (effective anon/authenticated privileges)
nodes.norm_label: production privilege check query (effective anon/authenticated privileges)
nodes.rationale: Run after every prepare, cutover and comment migration; it checks effective privileges, including PUBLIC, inherited and default grants, rather than ACL text, and any unexpected grant stops the next owner GO.

nodes.label: read_compatible_interpretations() View-Backing Function
nodes.rationale: Enforces auth.uid ownership internally; its EXECUTE grant is retained because PostgreSQL checks function calls in a view against the querying role, which the rehearsal proves by revoking it and expecting view SELECT to fail; if SELECT works without it, the grant is removed.

nodes.label: get-interpretation Read Cap (600/day) and No-Polling Client Contract
nodes.norm_label: get-interpretation read cap (600/day) and no-polling client contract
nodes.rationale: TASK-033 raises this endpoint's cap from 30 to 600 per user per UTC day on the shared increment_rate_limit counter because a read costs no model spend; the 3b client calls it once on open and once after generation and polls lab_reports.status instead, since a 3-second poll would exhaust the cap in 30 minutes.

nodes.label: SQL Full-Access Under-Reveal Relative to TypeScript
nodes.norm_label: sql full-access under-reveal relative to typescript
nodes.rationale: SQL (via the private interpretation_reader_is_full check) grants Full only with report ownership, a public users row and one provable source: a committed claim, a complimentary grant, an active Stripe subscription or an active production IAP row. Sandbox (even beta), grace, billing_retry, Stripe trialing/past_due, missing facts and SQL errors do not prove Full, so old binaries show Basic in those states while the TS-authoritative endpoint may return Full; support must expect this.

nodes.label: Stored Depth Classification and Legacy Backfill (deep / standard / unknown)
nodes.norm_label: stored depth classification and legacy backfill (deep / standard / unknown)
nodes.rationale: Neither row tier nor AI source is a Full entitlement; tier='plus' rows backfill as deep, pre-tiering rows qualify only with a nonempty overall_interpretation, and the rest stay unknown and request regeneration. Depth classifies availability, never the reader's access.

nodes.label: Verification Suites and Docker Migration Stop Conditions
nodes.norm_label: verification suites and docker migration stop conditions
nodes.rationale: Focused Vitest suites plus the Lead's Docker run of supabase/migrations/__verification__/run.sh are stop conditions, not source-only certification; SQL SELECT shape tests do not substitute for live PostgREST or physical old-binary checks, and the implementer sandbox cannot run Docker, network or Deno.

nodes.rationale: 90-minute timeout because the full V2 harness takes about 45 minutes; npm ci is required because without workspace dependencies the harness exits silently at test -x node_modules/.bin/vitest.

nodes.label: Preview job: merge the wave queue and run the gates
nodes.norm_label: preview job: merge the wave queue and run the gates
nodes.rationale: Each gate is continue-on-error so every outcome is recorded; a PR conflicting with main plus earlier PRs is left out and reported, fork heads are skipped, and nothing is pushed: the scratch commit exists only on the runner.

nodes.label: Report job: comment failures on the queue issue
nodes.norm_label: report job: comment failures on the queue issue

nodes.rationale: Complements ci.yml and e2e.yml; web e2e stays in e2e.yml and is not repeated here.

nodes.rationale: Runs on every PR to main (labels other than factory:* do not rebuild); Node 24 because the Capacitor 8 CLI requires Node >= 22.

nodes.rationale: Money-related and concurrency-sensitive: it decides who gets a paid AI interpretation for free. Its first migration passed review but would have broken DELETE FROM lab_reports because ON DELETE SET NULL is an UPDATE that the immutability trigger rejected; only running it caught that.

nodes.label: Open question: classifier-backed flagged trends in Basic
nodes.norm_label: open question: classifier-backed flagged trends in basic
nodes.rationale: flagged_trends now needs a classifier safety claim intersected with the model-flag rule, which only reduces Basic; showing unflagged out-of-range trends would move a premium item into Basic and needs an owner ruling.

nodes.label: Frozen Basic key allow-list (BASIC_KEYS)
nodes.rationale: Untouched by this task; Basic projections may contain only these keys, which forced the version marker into locked.

nodes.label: Proof 2: rejection cannot expand Basic (expansionViolations)
nodes.rationale: Across 8 model mutations Basic keeps keys within BASIC_KEYS, floor keys equal to legacy, entries as sub-objects of legacy entries and counts within authorized claims; backfilling or premium-key mutants fail it.

nodes.label: "char" catalog column concatenation defect (snapshot line 7)
nodes.rationale: claim-policy-gate.snapshot.sql concatenated pg_class.relkind, typed "char", so text || "char" had no unique operator; fixed with c.relkind::text.

nodes.label: Clinical claim record
nodes.rationale: Each claim carries claim_id, category, rule, fact, authority, policy_version v2-03c.1, recommendation_authority none and safety_authority, so provenance travels with every fact.

nodes.label: Open question: locked count can rise for falsely flagged markers
nodes.norm_label: open question: locked count can rise for falsely flagged markers
nodes.rationale: Legacy hid a wrongly flagged in-range trend as floor; it is now an ordinary authorized trend and is counted.

nodes.label: Finding A: compatibility view bypassed visibleClaimProjection
nodes.norm_label: finding a: compatibility view bypassed visibleclaimprojection
nodes.rationale: read_compatible_interpretations(), granted to authenticated, served legacy stored previews and inflated locked counts with no version check, so a direct query bypassed the TS gate.

nodes.label: Generated clinical movement policy kernel (clinical-movement-policy.generated.ts)
nodes.rationale: The server imports authority only from the generated kernel, never from src/; it must equal the client bytes and claim authority must equal createMovementClaim(...).authority, enforced by clinical:check and clinical:test.

nodes.label: Docker SQL harness Case 11 (claim-policy-gate)
nodes.rationale: claim-policy-gate.{prelude,capture,compare,verify,rollback,snapshot}.sql prove forward/verify on 16 fixture cases, replay idempotence, catalog coexistence, rollback twice, fresh chain and no widening; unexecuted until the Lead runs Docker.

nodes.label: JSON-path arithmetic precedence defect (prelude line 103)
nodes.rationale: e.c->'claim_preview' - 'claim' parsed as e.c -> ('claim_preview' - 'claim') because PostgreSQL binds arithmetic tighter than ->; fixed by parenthesizing the path and casting the literal.

nodes.label: Debt: lab-insights outside claim authority
nodes.rationale: The sibling model function stays premium-gated and render-gated rather than claim-authorized.

nodes.label: Legacy row projection (unchanged floor, null preview, zero counts)
nodes.norm_label: legacy row projection (unchanged floor, null preview, zero counts)
nodes.rationale: No provenance means no authorized claim: rows without a valid claim-era set project the unchanged floor and are never mutated.

nodes.label: Open question: legacy upsell disappears until regeneration
nodes.norm_label: open question: legacy upsell disappears until regeneration
nodes.rationale: Pre-V2-03c Basic rows read with no preview and zero counts because they lack provenance; a reversible backfill from stored trend_evidence would be a separate operation.

nodes.label: Proof 7: no strengthening of server claims
nodes.norm_label: proof 7: no strengthening of server claims
nodes.rationale: Restatements with different values are rejected (values_disagree), model trend_evidence/findings/clinical_claims never reach storage, and five at-rest tamperings fail closed.

nodes.label: Owner R3 ferritin/TSH cases
nodes.rationale: Unflagged out-of-range ferritin gets no Basic line, falsely flagged in-range TSH is stripped and counted as locked, counts may rise 0 to 1 with the same preview, and a rising count never adds a preview.

nodes.label: Proof 4: raw model output never renders as fallback
nodes.norm_label: proof 4: raw model output never renders as fallback
nodes.rationale: With no claims, preview is null and counts zero; legacy stored previews of model prose are not served, and unknown versions are neutralised.

nodes.label: Safety claim (analyte.reference_range_status)
nodes.rationale: One safety_alert per analyte that classifyAnalyte puts out_of_range, reusing the rule the deterministic writer maps to discuss; borderline maps to monitor, and no threshold was added or changed.

nodes.label: SAFETY_KEYS container pinning (six dimensions)
nodes.rationale: safety_notes, abnormal_flags, flags, warnings, critical_findings and what_to_do_next are probed with backed and unbacked lone objects; the first five become arrays keeping only backed flags, next steps are served as [].

nodes.label: Trend claim (trend_evidence.significant_change)
nodes.rationale: One factual_observation claim per buildTrendEvidence entry; its authority uses the generated kernel's MovementLanguage authority type so server and client agree.

nodes.label: TS/SQL claim-gate parity check
nodes.rationale: Vitest reads the SQL prelude fixture and checks TS outputs, the known-version list against KNOWN_CLAIM_POLICY_VERSIONS and byte-exact rollback; a pass-through TS mutant fails 9 tests.

nodes.label: Split claim-policy version markers
nodes.rationale: Full uses clinical_claims.policy_version and revalidates the whole set, stored Basic and SQL use locked.claim_policy_version without revalidating Full, and a root field confers nothing; a split-marker canary served patterns=9 while projectBasic gave zero.

nodes.label: Proof 6: safety in both directions
nodes.rationale: A classifier-backed ferritin safety claim survives any model output, while model attention, injected safety/critical booleans or forged clinical_claims cannot manufacture a safety claim for in-range TSH.

nodes.label: Claim-era version marker (locked.claim_policy_version)
nodes.rationale: BASIC_KEYS could not change, so the marker sits inside the existing locked object and is stripped from every response; no known version means legacy, and a known version still needs a claim-shaped preview.

nodes.label: Compatibility-view claim gate (interpretation_claim_gate)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors visibleClaimProjection/servedBasic in SQL: only claim-shaped previews and positive-integer counts survive a known version; the Basic branch becomes gate(sanitize_basic(...)), the gate is revoked from client roles and no row is rewritten.

nodes.label: Latent divergence: extreme-integer locked counts
nodes.rationale: TS Number.isInteger and SQL numeric/trunc diverge above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; unreachable while only service-role save_interpretation writes bounded counts.

nodes.label: Inferred-type operand defect family
nodes.rationale: Both defects are one class (an inferred operand type feeding an overloaded operator), so the guard targets the family with one rule per known shape instead of the instance.

nodes.label: Lead-run verification gates (Docker harness, check:functions, browser suites)
nodes.norm_label: lead-run verification gates (docker harness, check:functions, browser suites)
nodes.rationale: The implementer sandbox has no Docker, network or localhost binding (listen EPERM), so these gates are deferred to the Lead and never self-certified.

nodes.label: Legacy protection gap (legacy projectBasic branch skips safety stripping)
nodes.norm_label: legacy protection gap (legacy projectbasic branch skips safety stripping)
nodes.rationale: Safety stripping protects only validated claim-era bodies; pre-V2-03c rows keep unauthorized safety assertions and rely on render-time gating, so the gap went to the owner as backlog.

nodes.label: No-backfill rule for rejected claims
nodes.rationale: After rejection, preview and counts equal those of the model-free payload; a rejected slot stays empty rather than being refilled from legacy content.

nodes.label: Lone safety object normalized to one-element array
nodes.norm_label: lone safety object normalized to one-element array
nodes.rationale: The authority strip handled arrays only while basicSafetyValue returns a lone object for object-shaped SAFETY_KEYS, so the object is normalized before the check; this is an observable API container change.

nodes.label: Server-owned interpretation keys (trend_evidence, findings, clinical_claims, claim_audit)
nodes.norm_label: server-owned interpretation keys (trend_evidence, findings, clinical_claims, claim_audit)
nodes.rationale: Dropped from the zod-stripped model payload and always rewritten by the server, so a model cannot add, replace or strengthen claims.

nodes.label: Latent divergence: claim-policy version semantics
nodes.rationale: visibleClaimProjection accepts every known version but storedClaimSet re-issues under the current one, so with a second version Full readers of older rows would lose preview and counts; a version-indexed validator is the suggested fix.

nodes.label: Intermediate-state limitation: hidden Full set unvalidated in TS
nodes.norm_label: intermediate-state limitation: hidden full set unvalidated in ts
nodes.rationale: The RPC selects Basic before TypeScript sees it, so a legacy or future-policy Full paired with a current Basic marker can evade classification; turn 3 must classify Full inside SQL before entitlement selection.

nodes.label: clinical_range_reviews table

Keyed by slug, population, phase, kind, candidate_id (UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT) and refuses SAFE by CHECK. No composite FK because MATCH SIMPLE skips NULL-phase rows; the forward requires an exact bijection with the frozen shipping identities instead, and the slug FK forces rollback order V2-03 then V2-01.
